thm-offline-coverage-impossibility-examp:
## Statement

There are two finite one-step Markov decision processes with the same logged-data law under one behavior policy, but different target-policy values and different uniquely optimal actions. A finite one-step Markov decision process here has a finite state set, finite nonempty action sets, a finite reward set, and a probability mass on the next-state/reward pair for every state/action pair. Let the state set be $\{s_0,z\}$, the action sets be $A(s_0)=\{a,b\}$ and $A(z)=\{c\}$, the reward set be $\{-1,0,1\}$, and the horizon be $H=1$. In both processes, action $a$ at $s_0$ gives reward $0$ and moves to $z$, and action $c$ at $z$ gives reward $0$ and stays at $z$. In process $M_+$, action $b$ at $s_0$ gives reward $1$ and moves to $z$; in process $M_-$, it gives reward $-1$ and moves to $z$. The behavior policy chooses $a$ at $s_0$ with probability $1$, while the target policy chooses $b$ there with probability $1$; both policies choose $c$ at $z$ with probability $1$. Every behavior-generated logged trajectory is $(s_0,a,0,z)$ in both processes, so every sample size $n\ge1$ has the same logged-data law in $M_+$ and $M_-$. The target value is the expected one-step reward: it is $1$ in $M_+$ and $-1$ in $M_-$, and the unique value-maximizing initial action is $b$ in $M_+$ and $a$ in $M_-$. An estimator here is a real-valued function of the logged dataset; it is unbiased for a target value when its expectation under the logged-data law equals that value. Consequently, no such estimator can be unbiased for the target value in both processes, and no data-based action selector can identify the unique optimal initial action with certainty in both.
def-offline-reinforcement-learning-datas:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the policy-induced path laws below. Let $S$ be a nonempty finite state set, let $A(s)$ be a finite nonempty action set for each $s\in S$, and let $\mathcal R\subset\mathbb R$ be a finite nonempty reward set. A finite Markov decision process here consists of these sets and a joint next-state/reward probability mass $p(s',r\mid s,a)\ge0$, defined for $s,s'\in S$, $a\in A(s)$, and $r\in\mathcal R$, with $\sum_{s'\in S}\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}p(s',r\mid s,a)=1$ for every $(s,a)$. A stationary Markov policy $\sigma$ assigns probabilities $\sigma(a\mid s)\ge0$ with $\sum_{a\in A(s)}\sigma(a\mid s)=1$ at every state.

Fix a horizon $H\ge1$, a discount $0\le\gamma\le1$, and an initial state $s_0\in S$. A trajectory is a tuple $\tau=(s_0,a_0,r_1,s_1,\ldots,a_{H-1},r_H,s_H)$ with $s_t\in S$, $a_t\in A(s_t)$, and $r_{t+1}\in\mathcal R$ for each $0\le t<H$. Write $\Omega_H$ for the finite set of all such tuples. For each stationary policy $\sigma$, let $P^\sigma_H$ be the probability law on $\Omega_H$ whose atom masses are

$$P^\sigma_H(\{\tau\})=\prod_{t=0}^{H-1}\sigma(a_t\mid s_t)p(s_{t+1},r_{t+1}\mid s_t,a_t).$$

For a trajectory $\tau$, its finite-horizon return is $G_H(\tau)=\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^t r_{t+1}$, and the value of target policy $\pi$ from $s_0$ is $J_H(\pi;s_0)=\int_{\Omega_H}G_H\,dP^\pi_H$. A fixed logged dataset of size $n\ge1$ consists of independent trajectories $(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_n)$, each with law $P^\mu_H$ for a behavior policy $\mu$; the true behavior propensities $\mu(a\mid s)$ used to generate the data are known. Full horizon coverage means $P^\pi_H\ll P^\mu_H$, so every behavior-null trajectory event is also target-null. In this finite setting, the condition $\pi(a\mid s)>0\Rightarrow\mu(a\mid s)>0$ at every state-action pair reachable under $\pi$ before time $H$ is sufficient for full horizon coverage. A trajectory function is integrable under a law $P$ when $\int_{\Omega_H}|f|\,dP<\infty$. All returns are integrable in this finite-horizon finite-reward setting; importance-weighted return expressions below are used only when they are integrable.
lem-finite-horizon-trajectory-ratio-is-r:
## Statement

Assume AC and the finite-horizon dataset conditions of the preceding definition, with full horizon coverage $P^\pi_H\ll P^\mu_H$. For $0\le t<H$, let $\Omega_{t+1}$ be the finite set of trajectory prefixes through $(R_{t+1},S_{t+1})$, and let $P^\sigma_{t+1}$ be the marginal law of this prefix under policy $\sigma\in\{\pi,\mu\}$. On a behavior-positive prefix define

$$W_{0:t}=\prod_{k=0}^{t}\frac{\pi(A_k\mid S_k)}{\mu(A_k\mid S_k)},$$

and set $W_{0:t}=0$ on behavior-null prefixes. Then $P^\pi_{t+1}\ll P^\mu_{t+1}$, and $W_{0:t}$ is a version of $dP^\pi_{t+1}/dP^\mu_{t+1}$ up to $P^\mu_{t+1}$-almost-everywhere equality. In particular, for every real $G$ integrable under $P^\pi_H$, the full-horizon weight $W_{0:H-1}$ satisfies

$$\mathbb E_{P^\mu_H}[W_{0:H-1}G]=\mathbb E_{P^\pi_H}[G],\qquad \mathbb E_{P^\mu_H}[W_{0:H-1}|G|]<\infty.$$

The same identity holds prefixwise: for each $0\le t<H$ and every real $g$ integrable under $P^\pi_{t+1}$, with $g$ evaluated on the observed prefix,

$$\mathbb E_{P^\mu_H}[W_{0:t}g]=\mathbb E_{P^\pi_H}[g],\qquad \mathbb E_{P^\mu_H}[W_{0:t}|g|]<\infty.$$
alg-trajectory-importance-sampling-ope:
## Definition

Assume AC for the policy-induced trajectory laws. Input a finite-horizon logged dataset of $n\ge1$ independent behavior trajectories, a target policy $\pi$, the true behavior propensities $\mu(a\mid s)$, horizon $H$, and discount $0\le\gamma\le1$. Require full horizon coverage $P^\pi_H\ll P^\mu_H$. For trajectory $i$, compute $\rho_{i,t}=\pi(A_t^i\mid S_t^i)/\mu(A_t^i\mid S_t^i)$ for $0\le t<H$, and $W_{i,t}=\prod_{k=0}^{t}\rho_{i,k}$; set $W_{i,-1}=1$. If an observed pair has $\mu(A_t^i\mid S_t^i)=0<\pi(A_t^i\mid S_t^i)$, return status unsupported; if both probabilities are zero, set that ratio to zero. Let $G_i=\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^tR_{t+1}^i$. Return the ordinary trajectory estimator

$$\widehat J_{\mathrm{OIS}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n W_{i,H-1}G_i,$$

the per-decision estimator

$$\widehat J_{\mathrm{PDIS}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^tW_{i,t}R_{t+1}^i,$$

and the self-normalized weighted estimator

$$\widehat J_{\mathrm{WIS}}=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{\sum_{i=1}^nW_{i,H-1}G_i}{\sum_{i=1}^nW_{i,H-1}},&\sum_{i=1}^nW_{i,H-1}>0,\\0,&\sum_{i=1}^nW_{i,H-1}=0.\end{cases}$$

All three outputs are finite under the finite-MDP, finite-horizon and coverage hypotheses. The procedure specifies estimators; it includes no finite-sample unbiasedness assertion for the self-normalized output.
alg-doubly-robust-ope:
## Definition

Assume AC for the behavior-policy trajectory law. Input a finite-horizon logged dataset with $n\ge1$ behavior trajectories, a target policy $\pi$, finite real functions $\widehat Q_t(s,a)$ for $0\le t<H$, and finite nonnegative action-weight multipliers $\widehat\rho_t(s,a)$ for $0\le t<H$. Hold the functions and multipliers fixed when taking expectation over the evaluation dataset; they may be conditioned on an independent training sample. Define $\widehat V_H(s)=0$ for every $s$, and for $t=H-1,\ldots,0$ define

$$\widehat V_t(s)=\sum_{a\in A(s)}\pi(a\mid s)\widehat Q_t(s,a).$$

For each logged trajectory $i$, set $\widehat W_{i,-1}=1$ and $\widehat W_{i,t}=\widehat W_{i,t-1}\widehat\rho_t(S_t^i,A_t^i)$ for $0\le t<H$. Compute

$$D_i=\widehat V_0(s_0)+\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^t\widehat W_{i,t}\left(R_{t+1}^i+\gamma\widehat V_{t+1}(S_{t+1}^i)-\widehat Q_t(S_t^i,A_t^i)\right),$$

and return $\widehat J_{\mathrm{DR}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD_i$. When supplied as propensity ratios, the multipliers have the form $\widehat\rho_t(s,a)=\pi(a\mid s)/\widetilde\mu_t(a\mid s)$, with positive denominators on target-positive actions. In the exact-ratio case they equal the target-to-behavior action-likelihood factors $\pi(a\mid s)/\mu(a\mid s)$; the procedure also permits finite fitted multipliers for the correct-value-model case. The fixed terminal value $\widehat V_H=0$ is part of the procedure.
thm-trajectory-importance-sampling-is-un:
## Statement

Assume AC and the finite-horizon dataset conditions with full trajectory coverage $P^\pi_H\ll P^\mu_H$, true known behavior propensities, and the integrability hypotheses in the dataset definition. Then the ordinary trajectory estimator and per-decision estimator returned by the preceding algorithm each have expectation $J_H(\pi;s_0)$ under the behavior-generated sample law. This statement makes no finite-sample unbiasedness claim for the self-normalized weighted estimator.
thm-doubly-robust-ope-is-unbiased-under-:
## Statement

Assume AC and the finite-horizon dataset conditions with fixed target policy $\pi$, behavior policy $\mu$, horizon $H$, discount $0\le\gamma\le1$, and initial state $s_0$. Hold the finite functions $\widehat Q_t$ and multipliers $\widehat\rho_t$ fixed when taking expectation over the evaluation trajectories. Set $\widehat V_H(s)=0$ and $\widehat V_t(s)=\sum_{a\in A(s)}\pi(a\mid s)\widehat Q_t(s,a)$. Let

$$D(\tau)=\widehat V_0(s_0)+\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^t\widehat W_{0:t}(\tau)\left(R_{t+1}+\gamma\widehat V_{t+1}(S_{t+1})-\widehat Q_t(S_t,A_t)\right),\qquad \widehat W_{0:t}=\prod_{k=0}^{t}\widehat\rho_k(S_k,A_k).$$

For a dataset of $n$ independent evaluation trajectories, let $\widehat J_{\mathrm{DR}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD(\tau_i)$. Then $\mathbb E[\widehat J_{\mathrm{DR}}]=J_H(\pi;s_0)$ under either of these separate conditions:

1. The full target trajectory law is absolutely continuous with respect to the behavior trajectory law, and every multiplier is the correct action ratio $\widehat\rho_t(s,a)=\pi(a\mid s)/\mu(a\mid s)$ on every behavior-positive state-action pair reachable before time $H$; the ratio is $0$ when $\pi(a\mid s)=0<\mu(a\mid s)$. No correctness assumption is imposed on the functions $\widehat Q_t$.

2. For every $0\le t<H$, state $s$, and action $a$, the value model is exact:

   $$\widehat Q_t(s,a)=Q_t^\pi(s,a):=\sum_{s'\in S}\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}p(s',r\mid s,a)\left(r+\gamma V_{t+1}^\pi(s')\right),\qquad V_H^\pi(s)=0,\qquad V_t^\pi(s)=\sum_{a\in A(s)}\pi(a\mid s)Q_t^\pi(s,a),$$

   so $\widehat V_t=V_t^\pi$ at every step, including the zero terminal value. This branch requires no trajectory coverage and no correctness assumption on the fixed finite multipliers. If neither exact condition holds, this theorem asserts no unbiasedness.
